# SWAP Development Instructions for AI Assistants
## Objective

Replace scattered SAVE/DATA patterns with explicit state types to enable:
- Multi-instance execution (multiple SWAP models in one process)
- Thread-safe parallelization
- Future GPU offloading capability
- BMI-compatible state management

## CRITICAL: Build System Rules

**ALWAYS use pixi for ALL commands** - Never run or build tools directly:
```bash
pixi run setup-ifx      # Setup Intel Fortran
pixi run build-linux    # Build for Linux  
pixi run build-windows-cross  # Cross-compile
pixi run test-linux-hupselbrook  # Run tests
pixi run clean          # Clean build
...
```
see pixi.toml for full list of commands.

Code Modification Constraints
Physics Protection (HIGHEST PRIORITY)

    NEVER modify equations, coefficients, or algorithmic logic in computational kernels

    NEVER change variable semantics or units

    Allowed: Interface improvements (kinds, intents), SAVE removal with explicit state passing

    When in doubt: Wrap legacy code, don't rewrite it

    Remember about properly initializing the state variables to avoid uninitialized data issues and moving the necessary variables to the variables.f90 as module-level bridge variables if needed (for the stage 1 at least).

    ALWAYS finish with creating tests, as before, add the testing workflow to pixi and update the REFACTORING_PLAN.md

## State Management (Current Refactoring Focus)

    Remove SAVE, DATA, COMMON statements

    Replace with explicit state passing via swap_state_t derived types

    Use module-level variables in variables.f90 as temporary bridge

    Add sync procedures in swap_state_sync.f90

    Pattern:

```fortran
    ! Before (BAD):
    real :: var
    save var

    ! After (GOOD):
    ! Add to swap_state_mod.f90: type(*_state_t) field
    ! Add to swap_state_sync.f90: bidirectional sync
    ! Add to variables.f90: module-level bridge variable
```
I/O Separation

    NO file I/O inside computational kernels

    Core routines operate only on arguments

    I/O allowed only in *_io_mod modules or driver layers

    Prefer in-memory operation for Python/BMI compatibility

Modern Fortran Requirements

    implicit none in every module/procedure

    use iso_fortran_env, only: real64, int32 for kinds

    Intent declarations on all arguments

    Document physical units in comments ! [mm/day]

Testing Requirements

Every code change MUST:

    Keep existing tests passing (run pixi list test-linux-*) 0 we can run the all regression tests, that checks the numerical results against the baseline

    Add new unit tests for the fortran code

    Use swap_log module for debugging (levels: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) (add logs)

When Suggesting Changes

Always consider:

    Does this change physics? → If yes, STOP and ask for confirmation

    Does this remove SAVE? → Add to state type + sync procedures

    Does this add I/O? → Move to separate *_io_mod or wrapper

    Is there a test? → Add one before implementing

    Does it use pixi? → Never bypass pixi for commands

Preferred response pattern:

    State what you understand about the constraint

    Propose the change with explicit state type modifications

    Show the sync procedure updates

    Suggest test coverage

    swap_state_sync.f90 - Add sync procedures

    variables.f90 - Add module-level bridge if needed

    tests/unit/[module]/test_*_state.f90 - Add tests
